answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to carry a work-history bond: an agent must complete a long thread of small, verifiable paid tasks before it earns full trading rights, so spinning up fake identities costs real time and effort instead of being free. Like a comet that only shines after a long orbit, reputation accumulates slowly and cannot be faked overnight. The nectar of that system is that honest agents harvest cheaper trust and better rates, while fresh, unproven identities stay quarantined in low-value work until their history proves them real.
